cat_keyboard: The cat has fallen asleep across the keyboard, purring into the warm keys, and the screen has dimmed itself out of politeness. Your work can wait; the cat has decided it can.
dusk_room: The light in the room has gone the colour of weak tea. Somewhere a clock ticks slower than it should. The chair by the window is still warm from the afternoon, and nobody is asking anything of you.
dust_sunbeam: Dust turns slowly in a shaft of afternoon sun, gold on gold, and the room is so quiet you can hear the house settling, timber and plaster letting go of the day.
kettle: The kettle has just come off the boil and stands ticking on the stove, steam thinning into the cold kitchen air. The cup beside it is already warm in your hands.
library: The library after closing: chairs pushed in, lamps still lit in pools along the tables, the smell of old paper and rain on coats. Somewhere a page turns by itself in the draught.
porch_swing: The old porch swing moves a little in the evening air, chains creaking once, then still. Fireflies are starting up over the grass, and the day is folding itself away.
rain_roof: Rain on the tin roof, steady as a hand on a shoulder. Inside, the lamp hums low and the tea has gone cool enough to hold. Nothing out there needs you tonight.
snow_fence: Snow is settling on the fence posts, one flake at a time, until each post wears a small white cap. The fields beyond are blank and silent, and the whole world seems to have agreed to rest.
